For this study as well as the study in section 6, we recruit participants through Prolific. Participants are required to be fluent in English and are based primarily in English-speaking countries.
guideline: Annotators evaluate sufficiency and faithfulness of rationales on Likert scales; provide natural language feedback; rate ease of repair; and in Study 2, rate interpretability, trustworthiness, and importance of rationale properties.

Annotators rate interpretability (benefit for understanding) and trustworthiness (likelihood to trust answer) on Likert scales; they also rate importance of rationale properties such as attribution, depth of reasoning, sequential reasoning, strictness, and conciseness.

Annotators evaluate if the rationale provides enough information to answer the question, without the context. Annotators evaluate whether the rationale accurately draws conclusions from the context without misrepresenting any information.
